key_insight: The paper combines neural implicit representations with a factorized Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) to learn compact, parametric flows: spatial modes are represented implicitly while parameter- and time-dependence are separated and propagated linearly in a learned latent DMD space. This yields accurate, efficient predictions across parameter variations without needing explicit governing equations.
problem_solved: How to build fast, low-dimensional, data-driven models that generalize across continuous parameter changes for high-dimensional, nonlinear dynamical systems where traditional solvers or fixed reduced bases fail.
method: Learn neural implicit representations of system state (continuous spatial field) conditioned on parameters and time.
Factorize the representation into shared spatial modes and parameter/time-dependent coefficients.
Apply a learned DMD/linear operator in the coefficient (latent) space to propagate dynamics and enable interpolation/extrapolation across parameters.
impact: Provides practitioners a scalable, physics-agnostic reduced-order modeling tool for real-time prediction, control, and parameter studies of complex dynamical systems, reducing compute cost while retaining accuracy over parameter variations.

paper_title: Factorized Neural Implicit DMD for Parametric Dynamics
paper_authors: Siyuan Chen, Zhecheng Wang, Yixin Chen, Yue Chang, Peter Yichen Chen
